recipe: Saffron chicken pilaf with sultanas, almonds & mint yoghurt
servesNote: 2 portions — 890 kcal / 68 g protein each at £1.84/portion. ⭐ Converts the two cheapest things in the kitchen — bone-in thighs and the rice already on the shelf — into something that reads as special-occasion Persian rather than budget one-pot.
adaptations: ✅ THIS IS THE ONE YOU CAN VIRTUALLY COOK TONIGHT. Tuesday bought the bone-in thighs, onions, garlic, Greek yoghurt and lemons, and the saffron (4 sachets), chicken stock, mint sauce, flaked almonds and rice are all in the cupboard. Nothing here depends on a paste sachet that ran out.

⚠️ SULTANAS ARE DOWN TO 30 g, which is exactly what this takes and leaves none. ⛔ If they have gone, SKIP them — do not substitute jam-sweet dried fruit, which pushes the dish sweet in a way the mint yoghurt cannot pull back.
⚠️ MINT SAUCE: three sachets left after the lamb spends its three, and this takes one. Best before Sep–Oct, and this is one of only two dishes that uses them.

⭐ THE SKIN COMES OFF, and that is deliberate. Skin trapped under a lid goes flabby, so recipes that keep it have to rescue it under a grill afterwards. Removing it costs nothing in flavour here and takes ~250 kcal a portion off.

ingredients.prep: ⭐ SKIN PULLED OFF, patted properly dry
the mint yoghurt — ⭐ served alongside so it stays white against the saffron
half squeezed into the rice at the end, the rest in wedges
⛔ rinsed until nearly clear, and DO NOT SOAK
⭐ bloomed FIRST — 15 minutes is more than 5
⚠️ taste and correct the liquid BEFORE the lid goes on
toasted dry, straight out onto a plate

equipment.why: ⛔ the lid must sit TIGHT — foil under it if it is loose
⭐ blooming the saffron in just-boiled water
rinsing the rice, raking with your fingers
⭐ gripping the skin — it comes off each thigh in one
⭐ laid flat over the pan under the lid for the 10-minute rest
⛔ forking the rice from the outside inwards — lifting and turning, never stirring

prep: ⭐ Crumble the saffron into a mug with 3 tbsp just-boiled water and leave it while you do everything else. You want it to go from pale yellow to deep orange — 15 minutes is more than 5. Dry threads stirred into a pot give colour to two grains and nothing to the rest.
Rice into a sieve, rinse under cold water raking with your fingers until the water runs from milky to almost clear (4–5 passes). Drain. ⛔ Do NOT soak.
Pull the skin off each thigh — grip it with kitchen paper and it comes away in one. Pat the meat properly dry and season all over. A wet surface steams; a dry one browns.

steps.text: Heat the oil in the wide lidded pan over medium-high until it shimmers and thins out. Lay the thighs in smoothest side down, in a single layer with gaps. Leave them completely alone until they release from the pan without tugging and the underside is deep gold — lifting early tears the crust off. Turn, 2–3 min, out. ⚠️ They are not cooked through; they finish in the rice.

Drop to medium. Onion + a pinch of salt, stirring and scraping the browned residue off the base as the onion's moisture loosens it, until the slices have collapsed, gone floppy and turned properly golden-brown at the edges — not merely translucent. ⭐ This caramelised sweetness is the backbone, and it is the step most weeknight versions cut to four minutes.
Garlic, cumin seeds, cinnamon, turmeric. One minute, until the cumin smells toasted and nutty and the onion is stained yellow.
Drained rice in, stir a further minute until every grain is coated in fat and glossy and the edges look chalky-opaque. ⭐ This is what makes it a pilaf rather than boiled rice with things in it.

Sultanas, bay, then the saffron water threads and all and the hot stock. ⭐ Taste the liquid and correct it NOW: it should taste slightly saltier than you would want to drink, because the rice will absorb all of it. Bring to a visible simmer.

Nestle the thighs on top, browned side up, pressed lightly into the surface but sitting ON the rice, not buried in it. Lowest heat, lid on tight. ⛔ No lifting and no stirring, until the liquid is gone — to check, tilt the pan: no free liquid should pool at the edge. ⚠️ Still visibly wet late on? Poke steam holes to the base with a spoon handle.
⭐ Off the heat entirely. Lay a clean tea towel flat across the top of the pan and put the lid back on over it. 10 minutes, undisturbed.
Meanwhile: yoghurt + mint sauce + a squeeze of lemon + a pinch of salt, loosened with a teaspoon of water if stiff.
Separately toast the almonds in a dry pan, shaking constantly until patchily gold and nutty — straight out onto a plate, they keep colouring in the hot pan and go bitter.

Chicken onto a plate. ⭐ Fork the rice from the outside inwards, lifting and turning rather than stirring, and scrape up whatever has caught on the base — the crisp layer is a prize, not a mistake. Squeeze in half the lemon, check the salt. Serve with the chicken on top, almonds scattered, mint yoghurt alongside, lemon wedges at the table. ⚠️ Maria's next-day lunch: cool it fast — spread out, not in a deep sealed tub — fridge within the hour, and reheat piping hot. Cooked rice is the one leftover worth being disciplined about.
